Title: "SonicWall NSM On-Prem Affected By Multiple Vulnerabilities"
Description: ""1) CVE-2026-96540 - SonicWall NSM On-Prem Improper Access Control Vulnerability An improper access control vulnerability has been identified in the SonicWall Network Security Manager (NSM) on-prem in export settings, potentially allowing a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information. This may allow the attacker to escalate privileges to an administrator or to intercept communications of other users of the NSM instance. CVSS Score: 8.8 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization 2) CVE-2026-100232 - SonicWall NSM On-Prem Authenticated OS Command Injection Vulnerability Post-authentication Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability has been identified in the SonicWall Network Security Manager (NSM) on-prem which in specific conditions could potentially enable a remote authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands, resulting in remote code execution. CVSS Score: 7.2 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command SonicWall strongly advises users of the Network Security Manager (NSM) On-Prem (VMWare, Hyper-V, Azure and KVM) to upgrade to the mentioned fixed release version to address these vulnerabilities. There is currently no evidence any of the vulnerabilities addressed in this release are being exploited in the wild and NSM SaaS versions are not affected by these vulnerabilities. CVE: CVE-2026-96540, CVE-2026-100232 Last updated: Oct. 14, 2026, 6:50 a.m.""

Title: "PHP core RCE vulnerability patches (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)"
Description: ""CVSSv3 Score: 9.8 CVE-2026-109618PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).CVE-2026-109619PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE). Revised on 2026-10-23 00:00:00""

Description: ""Security is foundational to how Ivanti builds, tests, and supports our products. We continue to strengthen our secure product development practices through vulnerability discovery, responsible disclosure processes, security testing, threat-informed hardening, and coordinated response programs. Additionally, we recognize the importance of clear, timely communication when security issues arise. To that end, today we are disclosing a vulnerability in limited versions of Ivanti Connect Secure. At the time of disclosure, Ivanti is aware of limited exploitation in the wild. We are working directly with those organizations while making information, updates and remediation available to the broader customer community. If you are running one of the impacted versions, Ivanti recommends you act immediately. Additional information related to the impacted versions and remediations can be found in the Security Advisory: Ivanti Connect Secure Customers should review the security advisory, upgrade to the fixed version as soon as possible, and run the Integrity Checker Tool regularly. As with any security update, applying the fix is an essential step; however, it should be part of a layered security approach that includes strong access controls, network monitoring, log review, and ongoing validation of appliance integrity. Patch Tuesday Disclosures As part of our regular security program, Ivanti releases standard security patches on the second Tuesday of every month. At the time of disclosure, Ivanti is not aware of exploitation in the wild, and the fixes have been released. More information can be found in the Security Advisories: Ivanti Neurons Patch for Intune Xtraction Our Support team is always available to help customers and partners should they have any questions. Cases can be logged via the Ivanti Innovators Hub (login credentials required). Want to stay up to date on Ivanti Security Advisories?
